lean.statement: It is not the case that for every measure mu on the real line and every two functions f and g from the real line to itself, f equals g mu-almost everywhere implies that the classical gradients of f and g are equal mu-almost everywhere.
approved_definition_context: The gradient is Mathlib's total classical gradient of a real-valued function on the real line; no differentiability hypothesis is assumed by this negative statement.
Equality mu-almost everywhere means eventual equality in the almost-everywhere filter induced by the measure mu.
For a Dirac measure at a point, an almost-everywhere statement is determined by its value at that atom.
